macro.title: US‑Iran escalation heightens global risk premium
macro.body: Recent diplomatic warnings and the threat of Iranian retaliation after the US comments raise geopolitical uncertainty. Higher risk premia typically depress equity valuations worldwide, which could weigh on the US‑listed leveraged ETFs that dominate the portfolio.
macro.bull: If tensions de‑escalate quickly, risk appetite rebounds and leveraged ETFs benefit.
macro.base: Markets stay volatile but no major shock; leveraged ETFs trade sideways.
macro.bear: A sustained flare‑up triggers a flight to safety, pulling down high‑beta leveraged products.

macro.title: Eurozone energy policy delay lifts oil‑related equities
macro.body: The EU Parliament’s two‑year postponement of methane regulations reduces near‑term compliance costs for energy producers, supporting oil and gas stocks. The portfolio’s exposure to ENB.TO and SHEL may see modest upside.
macro.bull: Energy stocks rally on lower regulatory headwinds.
macro.base: Energy sector remains flat as broader market drivers dominate.
macro.bear: If the EU later reinstates stricter rules, energy margins could compress.

macro.title: US labour market resilience keeps Fed tightening on the table
macro.body: Weekly jobless claims edged up but remain low, signalling a still‑tight labour market. The Fed may keep rate hikes as an option, sustaining a strong USD. A stronger USD lifts the CAD‑converted value of the portfolio’s USD‑denominated holdings.
macro.bull: Continued USD strength adds CAD value to US‑listed positions.
macro.base: Fed holds rates steady; USD/CAD drifts modestly.
macro.bear: Unexpected rate cuts weaken the USD, eroding CAD value of US assets.

risks.title: Leverage Decay Volatility Spike
risks.context: 3x leveraged ETFs represent $133,909 CAD (51% of portfolio). VIX currently >22 increases decay risk.
risks.body: If market volatility stays elevated, the daily compounding effect will erode the value of SPXL, FNGU, UDOW and SOXL, potentially offsetting gains from any upside moves.

risks.title: USD/CAD Weakening Exposure
risks.context: USD notional $130,793 USD (≈ $187,426 CAD). A 0.01 fall in USD/CAD reduces CAD value by $1,308.
risks.body: A sustained decline in the USD relative to the CAD would diminish the CAD value of all US‑denominated holdings, notably the leveraged ETFs and NVDA.

risks.title: Single‑Stock Tail Risk – Broadcom Concentration
risks.context: AVGO position is $4,074 CAD (1.6% of portfolio).
risks.body: Broadcom’s earnings are increasingly tied to AI compute spend; a miss on its AI‑related guidance could cause a sharp drop, disproportionately affecting the portfolio given the concentration.

news.headline: Anthropic IPO fuels AI hype, lifts Nvidia and Broadcom
news.body: Anthropic’s $81 billion IPO underscores massive AI capital inflows. Nvidia (NVDA) and Broadcom (AVGO) are direct suppliers of compute power, so the market sentiment boost could lift their shares.

outcomes.label: Bull
outcomes.scenario: AI spending accelerates, Nvidia and Broadcom rally 8‑10%.

outcomes.label: Base
outcomes.scenario: Shares rise modestly 3‑4% as hype stabilises.

news.headline: US weekly jobless claims edge up, labour market stays tight
news.body: The modest rise in claims signals a still‑tight labour market, keeping the Fed’s tightening options open. A stronger USD benefits the CAD value of US‑listed leveraged ETFs.
news.exposure: SPXL $51,990 CAD, FNGU $43,128 CAD, UDOW $17,411 CAD, SOXL $21,380 CAD

outcomes.label: Bull
outcomes.scenario: USD strengthens 0.02 CAD, adding $2,616 CAD to USD‑denominated holdings.

outcomes.label: Base
outcomes.scenario: USD/CAD holds steady; leveraged ETFs move with market direction.

outcomes.label: Bear
outcomes.scenario: Unexpected rate cut weakens USD 0.02 CAD, costing $2,616 CAD.

news.headline: EU delays methane regulation, boosting oil & gas stocks
news.body: The two‑year postponement reduces compliance costs for energy producers, offering a tailwind to ENB.TO and SHEL.

outcomes.label: Bull
outcomes.scenario: Energy stocks climb 5% on regulatory relief.

outcomes.label: Base
outcomes.scenario: Markets price in the delay; stocks flat.

outcomes.label: Bear
outcomes.scenario: Later EU tightening triggers a 4% pull‑back.

picks.thesis: AMD benefits from the renewed US‑China semiconductor equipment easing and from strong demand for AI‑optimized GPUs, offering a non‑leveraged tech exposure to complement the existing semiconductor bets.
picks.entry: Target entry around $110‑$115 USD per share; monitor the next earnings release (Q4 2026) for catalyst.

picks.thesis: Lululemon’s recent brand‑renewal and strong international sales provide a high‑growth Canadian equity that adds consumer‑discretionary exposure without adding USD FX risk.
picks.entry: Consider buying on pull‑back to the $85‑$90 CAD range; watch Q3 earnings for margin trends.

picks.thesis: A dividend‑heavy telecom with stable cash flow, BCE can serve as a defensive anchor and generate CAD‑denominated income while the investor prepares for a home purchase.
picks.entry: Look for entry near $55 CAD as the stock approaches its 52‑week low; aim for a 4‑5% yield.

strengths.text: Core AI exposure with a $8,670 CAD position that is untouchable per investor mandate, providing upside in the sector.
High‑beta exposure to the FAANG+ universe ($43,128 CAD) that can capture rapid tech rally gains.
Tax‑deferred shelter for USD‑denominated assets, allowing the $21,079 CAD RRSP balance to grow without immediate Canadian tax.
Allocated $46,693 CAD for future home purchase; the FHSA holds Canadian equities (ENB, etc.) that are insulated from USD/CAD moves.
Low overall cash drag ($1,482 CAD total) preserves capital for opportunistic additions.

concerns.text: Uninvested RRSP cash ($112 CAD) is minimal, but any future contributions will sit idle unless allocated promptly.
Four 3x ETFs together form a concentration risk; a market correction could disproportionately affect more than half of portfolio value.
Large USD notional ($130,793 USD) means the portfolio is vulnerable to CAD appreciation, which would reduce CAD‑denominated value of most holdings.
Some positions (e.g., GBTC, BYDDF) have lower daily volume, potentially increasing execution cost if rapid rebalancing is needed.
Account rule constraint: No new contributions can go to FHSA/TFSA this year, limiting flexibility for tax‑advantaged growth.

strategy_short.text: Monitor VIX; if it stays above 22 for two consecutive weeks, trim $10,000 CAD of leveraged ETF exposure to curb decay risk.
Deploy the $112 CAD RRSP cash plus any near‑term bonus into the new AMD position to add non‑leveraged AI exposure.
Set stop‑loss alerts on AVGO at a 12% decline to manage single‑stock tail risk.

strategy_mid.text: Rebalance 15% of the leveraged ETF allocation into high‑quality Canadian dividend stocks (e.g., BCE, BMO) to reduce FX exposure and increase cash flow.
Build a modest CAD‑denominated cash buffer (~$5,000 CAD) in the Investment account for future FHSA contributions once the non‑resident status ends in 2027.
Evaluate adding a low‑cost global REIT ETF (e.g., VNQ) to diversify away from tech concentration while preserving growth potential.

strategy_long.text: Gradually shift a portion of the 3x leveraged exposure into a diversified core equity basket (e.g., a total market index fund) to lower volatility as the investor approaches the home‑purchase horizon.
Maintain the FHSA as a dedicated vehicle for the down‑payment, ensuring contributions are made once the 2027 residency status resumes, to maximize the $5,000 annual contribution room.
Plan for a partial exit from high‑beta tech positions (NVDA, FNGU) after the next major AI earnings season to lock in gains and reduce concentration risk.

tax.text: All new purchases must be routed to the RRSP to benefit from tax deferral; capital gains will be taxed upon withdrawal, which aligns with the investor's non‑resident status ending in March 2027.
Because the FHSA contribution room is frozen for 2026, avoid any TFSA or FHSA deposits this year to stay compliant with CRA rules.
When the investor returns to Canada in 2027, consider a strategic RRSP withdrawal to fund the home down‑payment, taking advantage of the Home Buyers' Plan (HBP) to defer taxes.

recent.name: NVIDIA Corporation
summary: Nvidia posted stronger‑than‑expected third‑quarter results, delivering a blowout earnings print that revived optimism in the AI trade.
The company issued an upbeat revenue forecast for the upcoming period, signaling confidence in continued demand.
A concern highlighted was new U.S. export restrictions limiting remote access to advanced Nvidia chips for several countries, potentially impacting overseas data‑center sales.

recent.name: Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.
summary: Live Nation posted Q3 2026 revenue and EPS that beat Wall Street estimates, driven by strong live‑event demand with 170 million tickets sold and nearly 180 million fans projected for the year.
The company highlighted continued robust demand for live events and reaffirmed its outlook for a high‑attendance 2026 season, but did not disclose any new quantitative guidance in the coverage.
The earnings surprise was notable, with earnings exceeding expectations by roughly 12.7%, underscoring a stronger‑than‑expected profit performance.

recent.name: QUALCOMM Incorporated
summary: Revenue of $10.32 billion in calendar Q3 2026 beat Wall Street expectations but fell 8.4% year‑over‑year.
The company projected next‑quarter revenue of $10.8 billion at the midpoint, about 2.6% above analysts’ consensus, and warned that chip‑design margins are under pressure.
Investors were surprised by the margin warning and rising semiconductor input costs, which outweighed the revenue beat.

macro_history.title: Easing of US‑China tech export restrictions
macro_history.body: Recent diplomatic talks suggest a rollback of curbs on semiconductor equipment shipments to China. A softer stance would lift pressure on US tech earnings, benefitting broad market leveraged ETFs that dominate the portfolio.
macro_history.bull: US tech rebounds, lifting leveraged equity exposure.
macro_history.base: Modest easing keeps current valuations stable.
macro_history.bear: Partial reversal or new restrictions hit tech, dragging leveraged ETFs.

macro_history.title: Canadian housing market cools as mortgage rates stay high
macro_history.body: Persistently elevated mortgage rates are dampening buyer activity in the GTA, slowing home price growth. This reduces near‑term demand for financing, pressuring domestic banks that form a sizable portion of the portfolio.
macro_history.bull: Slower price growth eases credit risk for banks.
macro_history.base: Banks hold steady amid modest slowdown.
macro_history.bear: Further rate pressure hurts loan growth, hurting bank earnings.

macro_history.title: Global AI investment surge lifts AI‑heavy chip makers
macro_history.body: Capital inflows into AI infrastructure are accelerating worldwide, beyond the US. Companies that supply GPUs and networking chips stand to gain, directly boosting the portfolio’s core AI stocks.
macro_history.bull: AI spend drives earnings upside for Nvidia and peers.
macro_history.base: Steady AI demand sustains current valuations.
macro_history.bear: Supply bottlenecks or regulatory limits curb AI growth.

macro_history.title: US Dollar Strength Boosts CAD‑Denominated Portfolio Value
macro_history.body: The USD/CAD pair has risen from 1.42 to 1.44 this week, reflecting a stronger U.S. dollar on higher Treasury yields. All USD‑denominated holdings (e.g., SPXL, FNGU, NVDA) are therefore worth more in CAD, providing a currency head‑room gain for the portfolio.
macro_history.bull: If USD/CAD climbs another 0.02, the CAD value of USD assets rises further.
macro_history.base: A modest continuation of the current USD strength yields a modest gain.
macro_history.bear: A sudden USD weakening would erode the currency gain.

macro_history.title: Fed Signals More Rate Hikes Amid AI‑Driven Inflation Concerns
macro_history.body: Recent Fed minutes suggest additional tightening to curb inflationary pressures from AI‑related compute demand. Higher rates could dampen growth‑oriented equities, especially leveraged ETFs that track the S&P and Nasdaq.
macro_history.bull: If the Fed pauses, leveraged ETFs retain upside.
macro_history.base: A measured rate hike path leads to modest volatility.
macro_history.bear: Aggressive tightening spikes volatility, hurting 3x ETFs.

macro_history.title: European Banking Stress Raises Credit Risk Outlook
macro_history.body: New data show rising non‑performing loans in several German regional banks, prompting concerns about credit quality in the Eurozone. A deterioration could spill over to global risk sentiment, pressuring equity markets and widening credit spreads.
macro_history.bull: If stress remains contained, equity markets stay resilient.
macro_history.base: Moderate stress leads to sideways equity performance.
macro_history.bear: Escalation triggers risk‑off flow, hurting leveraged equity ETFs.

macro_history.title: Bank of Canada Holds Rates Amid Sticky Inflation
macro_history.body: The Bank of Canada kept its policy rate at 4.75% following minutes that highlighted persistent core inflation. A steady rate environment supports the Canadian dollar and reduces volatility for CAD‑denominated assets, but may keep domestic growth modest.
macro_history.bull: A stable rate cushions Canadian equities and supports the CAD, preserving the value of the portfolio’s CAD‑listed holdings.
macro_history.base: Rate hold maintains status quo for most positions with limited upside or downside.
macro_history.bear: If inflation proves more entrenched, the BoC could hike again, pressuring the CAD and raising borrowing costs for Canadian firms.

macro_history.title: Escalating US‑Iran Tensions Spike Geopolitical Risk
macro_history.body: Recent intelligence reports of heightened threats from Iran increase the probability of regional conflict, which could disrupt global oil supplies and elevate energy prices. Canadian energy exporters and global oil‑linked ETFs may see price swings.
macro_history.bull: Higher oil prices boost ENB.TO and SHEL, enhancing dividend yields.
macro_history.base: Energy markets may trade in a narrow band as the market digests the news.
macro_history.bear: Escalation could trigger a flight to safety, hurting risk assets and raising borrowing costs for leveraged ETFs.

macro_history.title: US Credit Conditions Tighten as Debt‑Ceiling Talks Stall
macro_history.body: Prolonged negotiations over the US debt ceiling raise concerns about a technical default, tightening credit spreads and increasing volatility in US equity markets. This environment adds pressure on leveraged 3x ETFs that magnify market moves.
macro_history.bull: If a resolution is reached, credit spreads could compress, supporting US equities and leveraged ETFs.
macro_history.base: Markets likely price in a near‑term resolution with limited impact.
macro_history.bear: A default scenario would trigger a sharp sell‑off, disproportionately hurting SPXL, FNGU and UDOW.

macro_history.title: Fed Policy Uncertainty Amid White House Hearing
macro_history.body: Recent reports that Fed Governor Michelle Cook may be excluded from a White House hearing have heightened uncertainty about the timing of the next rate move. A delayed cut would keep US rates higher for longer, supporting the dollar and pressuring growth‑sensitive equities.
macro_history.bull: If the hearing proceeds and signals a dovish stance, equity risk premiums could compress.
macro_history.base: Markets likely price in a modest pause with no immediate policy shift.
macro_history.bear: A hard‑line stance could trigger a sell‑off in high‑beta tech and leveraged ETFs.

macro_history.title: Canada CPI Surprise May Prompt Rate Re‑Evaluation
macro_history.body: Statistics Canada is expected to release a November CPI reading that could exceed the 2.1% target. A surprise upward move would increase the odds of a tighter Bank of Canada stance, affecting the CAD and domestic equities.
macro_history.bull: If inflation eases, the CAD could weaken, boosting the CAD value of USD‑denominated holdings.
macro_history.base: Inflation stays near target, leaving current policy unchanged.
macro_history.bear: Higher inflation forces a rate hike, pressuring growth stocks and raising financing costs.

macro_history.title: Oil Price Volatility From US Crude Stock Build
macro_history.body: Rising US crude inventories have pulled oil prices lower, creating headwinds for energy producers. Canadian energy stocks will feel the impact directly, while a weaker USD could offset some losses for CAD‑priced holdings.
macro_history.bull: A rebound in oil would lift ENB and SHEL earnings.
macro_history.base: Oil stabilises around current levels, leaving energy exposure unchanged.
macro_history.bear: Further price declines erode cash flow for energy names.
